name: Is mental health a universal human right?

content.title: Is mental health a universal human right?
content.summary: A note from our founding director for the mental health day

media.alt: Is mental health a universal human right?

content.text: As we observe World Mental Health Day, it is imperative that we reflect on a matter of profound significance: the status of mental health as a universal human right.

In an era defined by progress and enlightenment, it is incumbent upon us at the Brain & Mind Institute to champion the belief that mental health is a universal human right. With a deep understanding of the critical role brain health plays in individual and collective well-being, our Institute seeks to address the lingering stigma surrounding mental health issues. In the countries we serve, we spearhead a shift towards community-centric approaches, rooted in local contexts. Through tireless efforts in research, education, innovation and strategic partnerships and engagement, we strive to bridge gaps in knowledge and resources.

Today we ask, 'Is mental health a universal human right?"  In a world that champions inclusivity, pluralism and compassion, the unequivocal answer must resoundingly be yes. It is our collective duty to dismantle barriers, dispel stigmas, and fortify the foundations upon which mental health stands as an irrefutable human entitlement.

At the Brain & Mind Institute, we are committed to the cause of mental health advocacy, pledging our resources, influence, and intellect towards the realization of a world where every individual, irrespective of circumstance, is granted the opportunity to thrive mentally, emotionally, and spiritually.

Let us work towards a future where mental health is not a privilege reserved for a fortunate few, but a right for all.  Let us not blame and judge those suffering in silence, but offer them kindness and dignity they deserve.
Prof Zul Merali,  Founding Director, BMI
